κυνεω.def: κυνέω 1. to kiss, Hom., Eur., etc. 2. = προσκυνέω, Eur.

κυνηγεσια.def: κυνηγεσία (later form for κῠνηγέσιον (signf. II), Plut.) (from κῠνηγετέω)

κυνηγεσιον.gloss: a hunting-establishment, huntsmen and hounds, a pack of hounds
κυνηγεσιον.def: κῠνηγέσιον, ου, τό, I. a hunting-establishment, huntsmen and hounds, a pack of hounds, Hdt., Xen. II. a hunt, chase, pursuit, Xen.; so in pl., Eur. III. that which is taken in hunting, the game, Xen. (from κῠνηγετέω)

κυνηγετεω.def: κῠνηγετέω, (κυνηγέτης) I. to hunt, Ar., Xen., etc.:—metaph. to persecute, harass, Aesch. II. to quest about, like a hound, Soph.

κυνηγετησ.def: κῠν-ηγέτης, ου, a hunter, huntsman, Od., Eur., etc.; κυναγέτας ἀμφὶ πάλᾳ one who seeks the prize in wrestling, Pind.:—fem. κυνηγέτις, doric κῠναγέτις, ιδος a huntress, Anth.

κυνηγετικοσ.def: κῠνηγετικός, ή, όν (from κῠνηγέτης) of or for hunting, fond of the chase, Plat.:— ὁ κυνηγετικός [λόγος] name of Xenophon's work on Hunting.

κυνηγεω.def: κῠνηγέω, (κυνηγός) to hunt, chase, later form of κυνηγετέω, Plut.

κυνηγιον.def: κῠνήγιον, ου, τό, (= κυνηγέσιον,) the hunt, chase, Plut.

κυνθοσ.def: Κῡ́νθος, ὁ, Cynthus, a mountain in Delos, birth-place of Apollo and Artemis, Hhymn.:—hence Apollo is called Κύνθιος, and Κυνθο-γενής, born on Cynthus, Ar., Anth.

κυνιδευσ.def: κῠνῐδεύς, έως, a puppy (cf. λαγιδεύς, λυκιδεύς), Theocr.

κυνιδιον.def: κῠνίδιον, ου, τό, (Dim. of κύων,) a little dog, whelp, puppy, Ar., Plat., etc.

κυνιζω.def: κῠνίζω, (κύων) to play the dog: metaph. to live like a Cynic, belong to their sect, Luc.

κυνικοσ.def: κῠνῐκός, ή, όν (κύων) I. dog-like, Lat. caninus, Xen. II. Κυνικός, οῦ, a Cynic, as the followers of the philosopher Antisthenes were called, Plut.

κυνισκοσ.def: κῠνίσκος, ὁ, (κύων) 1. a young dog, puppy, Hdt. 2. metaph. a little Cynic, Luc.

κυνισμοσ.def: κῠνισμός, οῦ, ὁ, Cynical philosophy or conduct, Luc.

κυνοδουσ.def: κῠν-όδους, οντος, a canine tooth, Xen., etc.

κυνοδρομεω.def: κῠνο-δρομέω, (δρόμος) to run with dogs, Xen.

κυνοθαρσησ.def: κῠνο-θαρσής, ές (θάρσος) impudent as a dog, Theocr.

κυνοκεφαλοσ.def: κῠνο-κέφᾰλος, ον (κεφαλή) 1. dog-headed; οἱ Κυνοκέφαλοι, dog-heads, the name of a people, Hdt. 2. the dogfaced baboon, Plat., Luc. [κυνοκεφάλλῳ in Ar.]

κυνοκοπεω.def: κῠνο-κοπέω, (κόπτω) to beat like a dog, Ar.

κυνοσαργεσ.def: Κυνόσαργες Cynosarges, a gymnasium outside Athens, for the use of those who were not pure Athenians, Hdt., Dem., etc. (deriv. uncertain)

κυνοσουρα.def: κῠνός-ουρα, ἡ, dog's-tail, the Cynosure, a name for the constellation Ursa Minor, Arat.

κυνοσπαρακτοσ.def: κῠνο-σπάρακτος, ον (σπαράσσω) torn by dogs, Soph.

κυνουχοσ.def: κυν-οῦχος, ὁ, (ἔχω) I. a dog-holder, dog-leash, Anth. II. a dog-skin sack, used in hunting, Xen.

κυντεροσ.def: κύντερος, η, ον (comp. adj. formed from κύων) I. more dog-like, i. e. more shameless, more audacious, Hom.; more horrible, κύντερον ἄλλο ποτ’ ἔτλης Od. II. Sup. κύντατος, η, ον most audacious, Il., Hhymn.

κυνω.def: κυνώ a she-dog:—as prop. n. Κυνώ, Hdt.

κυνωπησ.def: κῠν-ώπης, ου, ὁ, (ὤψ) the dog-eyed, i. e. shameless one, Il.:—so fem.κῠνῶπις, ιδος, Hom.

κυοφορεω.def: κυο-φορέω, (κύω, φέρω) to be pregnant, Luc.

κυπαρισσινοσ.def: κυπαρίσσινος of cypress-wood, Od., Thuc. (from κῠπάρισσος)

κυπαρισσοσ.def: κῠπάρισσος, αττιξ -ιττος, ἡ, a cypress, Od., Hdt., etc.

κυπασσισ.def: κῠπασσίς, ίδος a short frock, Anth. (deriv. uncertain)

κυπειρον.def: κῠ́πειρον, ου, τό, a sweet-smelling marsh-plant, perh. galingale, used to feed horses, Hom.

κυπελλομαχοσ.gloss: at which they fight with cups
κυπελλομαχοσ.def: κῠπελλο-μάχος, ον (μάχομαι) at which they fight with cups (cf. Horace pugnare scyphis), Anth.

κυπελλον.gloss: a big-bellied drinking vessel, a beaker, goblet, cup
κυπελλον.def: κῠ́πελλον, ου, τό, a big-bellied drinking vessel, a beaker, goblet, cup, Hom. (deriv. uncertain)

κυπεροσ.def: κύπερος, ὁ, (prob. ionic for κύπειρος, Hdt.)

κυπριδιοσ.def: Κυπρίδιος, η, ον (Κύπρις) like Cypris, i. e. lovely, tender, Anth.

κυπριοσ.def: Κύπριος, η, ον I. of Cyprus, Cyprian, Hdt., etc. II. Κύπρια, τά, an Epic poem introductory to the Il., id.

κυπρισ.def: Κύπρις, [ῠ βψ νατυρε], ῐδος, ἡ, I. Cypris, a name of Aphrodite, from the island of Cyprus, where she was most worshipped, Il., Trag., etc. II. as appellat. love, passion, Eur., etc.

κυπρογενησ.def: Κυπρο-γενής, ές (γίγνομαι) Cyprus-born, of Aphrodite, Hhymn., etc.:—fem. Κυπρο-γένεια, ἡ, Pind.

κυπροσ.def: Κύπρος, ἡ, Cyprus, a Greek island on the S. coast of Asia Minor, Hom., etc.:—the Romans got from it the best copper, Lat. cyprium.

κυπταζω.gloss: to keep stooping, to go poking about, potter about
κυπταζω.def: κυπτάζω, (Frequent. of κύπτω) to keep stooping, to go poking about, potter about a thing, Ar., Plat.

κυπτω.def: κύπτω (Root ΚΥΠ) 1. to bend forward, stoop down, Hom., Hdt., etc.; θέει κύψας runs with the head down, i. e. at full speed, Ar.; κύψας ἐσθίει eats stooping, i. e. greedily, id.; κέρεα κεκυφότα ἐς τὸ ἔμπροσθεν horns bent forward, of certain African oxen, Hdt. 2. to hang the head from shame, Ar. 3. to bow down under a burden, Dem.

κυρβασ.def: Κύρβας, αντος (shortd. form of Κορύβας, q. v.)

κυρβασια.def: κυρβᾰσία, ἡ, a Persian bonnet or hat, with a peaked crown, prob. much like the τιάρα, Hdt.: the King alone wore it upright, Ar.

κυρβεισ.def: κύρβεις I. triangular tablets, fitted at the angles so as to form a pyramid of three sides, and having the earliest laws written on the sides, Ar., Plat. II. in sg. metaph. of a pettifogging lawyer, Ar.

κυρειοσ.def: Κύρειος, η, ον of Cyrus, Xen.

κυρεω.def: κυρέω (Mid. κύρομαι [ῡ] in act. sense) I. followed by a case, to hit, light upon: 1. c. dat. to light upon, meet with, fall in with, strike against, Il., Hes.:—of things, κυρεῖν τινι to befall or be granted to him, Soph., Eur. 2. c. gen. to hit the mark, like τυγχάνω, Aesch.:— to reach to or as far as, Hhymn.: to meet with, find, Aesch., Soph. b. to attain to, be master of, obtain, Lat. potiri, Hdt., Trag. 3. c. acc., like Lat. potiri, to obtain, reach, find, Aesch., Eur. II. without a case, to happen, come to pass, Trag. 2. to be right, hit the exact truth, Soph. 3. as auxil. Verb, like τυγχάνω with partic., to turn out, prove to be so and so, σεσωσμένος κυρεῖ Aesch.; ζῶν κυρεῖ Soph.; ἐχθρὸς ὢν κυρεῖ Eur.; with partic. omitted, it acts merely as the copula, to be, Trag.

κυρηβαζω.def: κῠρηβάζω, to butt with the horns: metaph., τὸ σκέλος κυρηβάσει he shall come butt against my leg, or my leg shall butt him, kick him, Ar. (Perh. akin to κυρίσσω.)

κυρηβια.def: κῠρήβια, ων, τά, husks, bran:—a bran-shop, Ar. (deriv. uncertain)

κυρηνη.def: Κυρήνη, ἡ, Cyrene, a Greek colony in Africa, Hdt.: —the people were called Κυρηναῖοι, and the country ἡ Κυρηναία, id.

κυρια.def: κῡρία, ἡ, (fem. of κύριος signf. b. 1. 2.)

κυριακοσ.def: κῡριακός, ή, όν (κύριος) of or for a lord or master: esp. belonging to the Lord (Christ); Κ. δεῖπνον the Lord's Supper, ἡ κυριακὴ ἡμέρα the LORD'S day, dies Dominica, NTest. (Assumed to be original of the Teutonic kirk, kirche, church; but how this Greek name came to be adopted by the Northern nations, rather than the Roman name ecclesia, has not been satisfactorily explained.)

κυριευω.def: κῡριεύω, 1. to be lord or master of people orof a country, c. gen., Xen. 2. to have legal power to do, c. inf., ap. Aeschin. (from κῡ́ριος)

κυριοσ.def: κῡ́ριος, η, ον (κῦρος) I. of persons, having power or authority over, lord or master of, c. gen., Pind., attic:— κύριός εἰμι, c. inf., I have authority to do, am entitled to do, Aesch., etc.; κυριώτεροι δοῦναι better able to give, Thuc. 2. absol. having authority, authoritative, supreme, κ. εἶναι to have authority, Plat.; τὸ κύριον the ruling power in a state, τὰ κύρια the authorities, Soph., Dem. II. not of persons, authoritative, decisive, dominant, supreme, δίκαι Eur.; μῦθος κυριώτερος of more authority, id., etc. 2. opp. to ἄκυρος, authorised, ratified, valid, νόμοι, δόγματα Dem.; κ. θέσθαι or ποιεῖσθαί τι to appoint by authority, Soph., Dem. 3. of times, etc., fixed, ordained, appointed, Hdt., Eur., etc.;—so, τὸ κύριον the appointed time, Aesch.:—at Athens, κυρία ἐκκλησία a regular or ordinary assembly, opp. to σύγκλητος ἐκκλησία (one specially summoned), Ar. 4. legitimate, regular, proper, Aesch. 5. of words, authorised, vernacular, Lat. proprius, Arist. B. as Subst.,

κύριος, ὁ, I. a lord, master, Lat. dominus, of gods, Pind., Soph., etc.: the head of a family, master of a house, Aesch., etc.:—later, κύριε was a form of respectful address, like our sir, NTest. 2. κυρία, ἡ, mistress or lady of the house, Lat. domina, Menand., etc. II. ὁ Κύριος, the Lord, = Hebr. Jehovah, Lxx.; in NTest. esp. of Christ.

κυρισσω.def: κῠρίσσω, (κόρυς) to butt with the horns, Plat.:—metaph. of floating corpses knocking against the shore, Aesch.

κυριωσ.def: κυρίως (adverb of κύριος) I. like a lord or master, authoritatively, Aesch. II. regularly, legitimately, properly, κ. ἔχειν to be fixed, hold good, id.; κ. αἰτεῖσθαι, suo jure, Soph., etc. III. of words, in their proper sense, Arist.

κυρμα.def: κύρμα, ατος, τό, (κύρω) I. that which one meets with or finds, i. e. booty, prey, spoil, Hom. II. of a person, one who gets booty, a swindler, Ar.

κυρνοσ.def: Κύρνος, ἡ, Cyrnus, old name of Corsica, Hdt.: οἱ Κύρνιοι id.

κυροσ.def: κῦρος, εος, I. supreme power, authority, Hdt., Thuc., etc. II. confirmation, validity, certainty, Soph.
Κῦρος, ὁ, 1. Cyrus: 1. ὁ πρότερος, the elder Cyrus, Hdt. 2. ὁ νεώτερος, the brother of Artaxerxes, Xen.

κυροω.gloss: to make valid, confirm, ratify, determine
κυροω.def: κῡρόω, (from κῦρος) 1. to make valid, confirm, ratify, determine, Lat. ratum facere, Hdt., Aesch., etc.:—Mid. to accomplish one's end, Plat.:—Pass. to be ratified, Hdt., attic:—generally, κεκύρωται τέλος the end hath been fixed or determined, Aesch.; πρὶν κεκυρῶσθαι σφαγάς before it has been accomplished, Eur.:—impers. c. inf., ἐκεκύρωτο συμβάλλειν it had been decided to fight, Hdt.; ἐκυρώθη ναυμαχέειν id. 2. κ. δίκην to decide it, Aesch.

κυρτευτησ.def: κυρτευτής, οῦ, one that fishes with the κύρτη, Anth.

κυρτη.def: κύρτη, ἡ, 1. a fishing-basket, Lat. nassa, Hdt.; κυρτός, ὁ, =κυρτευτής, Plat. 2. a bird-cage, Lat. cavea, Anth. (from κυρτός)

κυρτοσ.def: κυρτός, ή, όν curved, arched, of a wave breaking, Il.; ὤμω κυρτώ round, humped, id.; κ. τροχός Eur.

κυρτοω.def: κυρτόω, to curve or bend into an arch, κυρτῶν νῶτα, of a bull preparing to charge, Eur.; κ. λαίφεα Anth.:—Pass. to form a curve or arch, of a wave breaking, Od., Xen.

κυρωσισ.def: κῡ́ρωσις, εως (κυρόω) a ratification, Thuc., Plat.

κυστισ.def: κύστις, εως (κύω) the bladder, Il., Ar.

κυτισοσ.def: κῠ́τῐσος, ὁ, cytisus, a kind of clover, Theocr.

κυτμισ.def: κυτμίς, ίδος a kind of plaster, Luc.

κυτογαστωρ.def: κῠτο-γάστωρ, ορος, with capacious belly, Anth.

κυτοσ.def: κῠ́τος, εος, (κύω) 1. the hollow of a shield or breastplate, Aesch., Ar. 2. any vessel, a vase, jar, urn, Aesch., Soph., etc.; πλεκτὸν κ. a basket, Eur. 3. anything that contains the body, Soph.

κυτταροσ.def: κύττᾰρος, ὁ, (κύτος) 1. the cell of a comb of bees or wasps, Ar. 2. metaph., τοὐρανοῦ τὸν κ. the concave vault of heaven, id.

κυφαγωγοσ.gloss: with neck arched and head low
κυφαγωγοσ.def: κῡφ-ᾰγωγός, οῦ, ὁ, with neck arched and head low, of a horse, Xen.

κυφαλεοσ.def: κῡφᾰλέος, η, ον (poetic for κυφός, Anth.)

κυφοσ.def: κῡφός, ή, όν (κύπτω) bent forwards, bent, stooping, hump-backed, Od., Ar.

κυφων.gloss: the bent yoke of the plough
κυφων.def: κύφων, ωνος, (κῡφός) I. the bent yoke of the plough, Theogn. II. a sort of pillory in which criminals were fastened by the neck, Ar. 2. one who has had his neck in the pillory, a knave, Lat. furcifer, Luc.

κυψελη.gloss: any hollow vessel: a chest, box
κυψελη.def: κυψέλη, ἡ, any hollow vessel: a chest, box, Hdt., Ar.

κυψελιδαι.def: Κυψελίδαι, ῶν, οἱ, descendants of Cypselus, Theogn.

κυω.def: κύω, I. in pres. and imperf., of females, to conceive, Orac. ap. Hdt., Theogn., etc. 2. rarely c. acc. to be pregnant with a child, Xen. II. in aor1 ἔκῡσα, Causal, of the male, to impregnate, and mid. ἐκῡσάμην, of the female, to conceive, Hes.

κυων.def: κύων I. a dog or bitch, Hom., etc.; most commonly of hounds, id., etc.; the Laconian breed was famous, Soph.;— νή or μὰ τὸν κύνα was the favourite oath of Socrates, Plat.: cf. τραπεζεύς. II. as a word of reproach, to denote shamelessness or audacity in women, rashness, recklessness in men, Hom. 2. at Athens a nickname of the Cynics, Arist., Anth. III. the Trag. apply the term to the ministers of the gods; the eagle is Διὸς πτηνὸς κύων Aesch.; the griffins Ζηνὸς ἀκραγεῖς κύνες id.; the Bacchantes Λύσσης κ. Eur., etc. IV. a sea-dog, mentioned as a fish in Od. V. the dog-star, i. e. the dog of Orion, placed among the stars with its master, Il.

κωασ.def: κῶας a fleece, used as bedding, Hom., Hdt. (deriv. uncertain)

κωβιοσ.def: κωβιός, οῦ, ὁ, a fish of the gudgeon kind, Plat., etc.

κωδαριον.def: κωδᾰ́ριον, ου, τό, (Dim. of κώδιον, Ar.)

κωδεια.def: κώδεια, ἡ, the head, Il. (deriv. uncertain)

κωδιον.def: κώδιον, ου, τό, (Dim. of κῶας) a sheepskin, fleece, used for bedding, Ar., Plat.

κωδων.def: κώδων, ωνος, a bell, Aesch., Eur.:—in fortified towns an officer went round at night with a bell to challenge the sentries, and see that they were awake, Thuc.; ὡς κώδωνα ἐξαψάμενος like one with an alarm-bell in his hand, Dem.

κωδωνιζω.def: κωδωνίζω, (from κώδων) to prove by ringing, of money, Ar.

κωδωνοκροτοσ.def: κωδωνό-κροτος, ον ringing, jingling, as with bells, Eur.

κωδωνοφαλαροπωλοσ.gloss: with bells on his horses' trappings
κωδωνοφαλαροπωλοσ.def: κωδωνο-φᾰλᾰρό-πωλος, ον with bells on his horses' trappings, Ar.

κωδωνοφορεω.gloss: to carry the bell round, to visit the sentinels
κωδωνοφορεω.def: κωδωνο-φορέω, to carry the bell round, to visit the sentinels, Ar.:—Pass., ἅπαντα κωδωνοφορεῖται everywhere the bell goes round, i. e. the sentinels are being visited, id.

κωθων.def: κώθων, ωνος, a Laconian drinking-vessel, Ar.

κωκυμα.def: κώκῡμα, ατος, τό, a shriek, wail, Aesch., Soph. (from κωκύω)

κωκυτοσ.def: κωκῡτός, οῦ, ὁ, (from κωκύω) I. a shrieking, wailing, Il., Trag. II. Κωκῡτός, οῦ, ὁ, Cocytus, river of wailing (cf. Ἀχέρων), one of the rivers of hell, Od., etc.

κωκυω.def: κωκύω 1. to shriek, cry, wail, mostly of women, Hom. 2. to wail over one dead, Od., Aesch., Soph.

κωλαγρετησ.gloss: collector of the pieces at a sacrifice
κωλαγρετησ.def: κωλ-αγρέτης, -ακρέτης, ου, ὁ, (κωλῆ, ἀγρέω) collector of the pieces at a sacrifice, name of a magistrate at Athens, who had charge of the public table in the Prytaneion, and paid the dicasts, Ar.; κωλαγρέτου γάλα, comically for the μισθὸς δικαστικός, id.

κωλη.gloss: the thigh-bone with the flesh on it, the ham
κωλη.def: κωλῆ (κῶλον) the thigh-bone with the flesh on it, the ham, esp. of a swine, Ar., Xen.

κωληψ.def: κώληψ, ηπος, ἡ, (from κωλῆ) the hollow of the knees, Lat. poples, Il.

κωλιασ.def: Κωλιάς (sub. ἄκρα) Colias, a promontory of Attica, with a temple of Aphrodite there, Hdt., Ar.

κωλον.def: κῶλον, ου, τό, I. a limb, esp. the leg, Trag. 2. of plants, a limb or arm, Anth. II. a member of anything, as, 1. a member of a building, as the side or front, Hdt. 2. one limb or half of the race-course (δίαυλος), Aesch. 3. a member or clause of a sentence, Lat. membrum, Arist.

κωλυμα.def: κώλῡμα, ατος, τό, (κωλύω) I. a hindrance, impediment, Eur., Thuc. II. a defence against a thing, precaution, Thuc.

κωλυμη.def: κωλῡ́μη, ἡ, = κώλυμα, ἐπὶ κωλύμῃ for the purpose ofhindering, Thuc.

κωλυτεοσ.def: κωλῡτέος, ον (verb. adj. of κωλύω,) one must hinder, Xen.

κωλυτικοσ.def: κωλῡτικός, ή, όν preventive, Xen. (from κωλύω)

κωλυω.def: κωλύω to let, hinder, check, prevent: 1. c. acc. et inf. to hinder or prevent one from doing, Hdt., Soph., etc.; with a negative added, κ. τινὰ μὴ θανεῖν Eur., etc.:—Pass. to be hindered, τοῦ ὕδατος πιεῖν from drinking of the water, Plat.; κωλυόμεσθα μὴ μαθεῖν Eur.; rarely with part., μὴ κωλύωνται περαιούμενοι Thuc. 2. c. gen. rei, κ. τινά τινος to let or hinder one from a thing, Xen.; so, κ. τινα ἀπό τινος id. 3. c. acc. rei, to hinder, prevent, impede, Eur., Thuc.:—Pass., μηδὲ δαπάνηι κεκωλύσθω and let there be no hindrance by reason of expense, Thuc. 4. absol., ὁ κωλύσων one to hinder, Soph.; τὸ κωλῦον a hindrance, Xen. 5. often in 3 pers., οὐδὲν κωλύει there is nothing to hinder, c. acc. et inf., Hdt., Ar.:— οὐδὲν κωλύει, absol., as a form of assent, nothing hinders, be it so, Ar.

κωμα.def: κῶμα, ατος, τό, (κεῖμαι) deep sleep, slumber, Lat. sopor, Hom., Hes.

κωμαζω.gloss: to go about with a party of revellers, to revel, make merry
κωμαζω.def: κωμάζω (from κῶμα) (κῶμος) I. to go about with a party of revellers, to revel, make merry, Lat. comissari, Hes., Theogn., Eur., etc. 2. to go in festal procession, Pind., Dem. II. to celebrate a κῶμος in honour of the victor at the games, to join in festivities, Pind.; c. acc. cogn., ἑορτὰν κ. id. 2. c. dat. pers. to approach with a κῶμος, sing in his honour, id. 3. c. acc. pers. to honour or celebrate him in or with the κῶμος, id. III. to break in upon in the manner of revellers, κ. ποτὶ τὰν Ἀμαρυλλίδα Theocr.:—generally, to burst in, Anth.

κωμαρχησ.gloss: the head man of a village
κωμαρχησ.def: κωμ-άρχης, ου, ὁ, (κώμη, ἄρχω) the head man of a village, Xen.

κωμαστησ.def: κωμαστής, οῦ, (κωμάζω) 1. a reveller, Plat., Xen. 2. epith. of Bacchus, the jolly god, Ar.

κωμη.def: κώμη, ἡ, = Lat. vicus, a village or country town, opp. to a fortified city; properly a doric word, = attic δῆμος, Hes., Hdt.; κατοικῆσθαι κατὰ κώμας to live in separate villages (not in walled towns), of the Medes, Hdt.; so, of a country, κατὰ κώμας οἰκεῖσθαι to have its people distributed into villages, Thuc.

κωμητησ.def: κωμήτης, ου, ὁ, (κώμη) I. a villager, countryman, Plat., Xen. II. in a city, one of the same quarter, Lat. vicinus, Ar.; more loosely, χθονὸς κωμῆται dwellers in a land, Eur.

κωμικοσ.def: κωμῐκός, ή, όν Lat. comicus, = κωμῳδικός, Aeschin.

κωμοπολισ.def: κωμό-πολις, εως (κώμη) a village-town, i. e. a place not entitled to be called a πόλις, NTest.

κωμοσ.gloss: a village festival: a revel, carousal, merry-making
κωμοσ.def: κῶμος, ου, (κώμη) I. properly a village festival: a revel, carousal, merry-making, Lat. comissatio, Hhymn., Theogn., etc.: it ended in the party parading the streets crowned, bearing torches, singing, dancing, and playing frolics, Ar. II. a band of revellers, a jovial troop, Eur.:—metaph. a rout, band, κ. Ἐρινύων Aesch.; of an army, Eur., etc. III. the ode sung at one of these festive processions, Pind.

κωμυσ.def: κώμῡς, ῡθος, ἡ, a bundle of hay, Lat. manipulus, Theocr. (deriv. uncertain)

κωμωδεω.gloss: to represent in a comedy, to satirise, lampoon, libel
κωμωδεω.def: κωμῳδέω (κωμῳδός) I. to represent in a comedy, to satirise, lampoon, libel, Ar., Plat.:—Pass. to be so satirised, Ar. 2. κωμωιδεῖν τὰ δίκαια κωμωιδοῦντα εἰπεῖν τὰ δ., id. II. to write comedies, Luc.

κωμωδια.def: κωμ-ῳδία, ἡ, a comedy, Ar., etc.:—Two derivs. are suggested: one from κῶμος, ᾠδή, the revel-song; the other from κώμη, ᾠδή, the village-song. There were three periods of Attic Comedy, Old, Middle, New, — παλαιά, μέση, νέα. The Old Comedy was used to attack by name the most powerful persons of the day, ending B. C. 393; the Middle Comedy lost the chorus, but still attacked notabilities under assumed characters, ending B. C. 337; the New was our Comedy of Manners, and may be best understood from Plautus and Terence.

κωμωδικοσ.def: κωμῳδικός, ή, όν (from κωμῳδία) of comedy, comic, Ar.

κωμωδοδιδασκαλια.def: κωμῳδοδῐδασκᾰλία, ἡ, the comic poet's art, Ar. (from κωμῳδοδῐδάσκᾰλος)

κωμωδοδιδασκαλοσ.def: κωμῳδο-δῐδάσκᾰλος, ὁ, a comic poet, because he had to train the actors and chorus, Ar.

κωμωδολοιχεω.gloss: to play the parasite and buffoon
κωμωδολοιχεω.def: κωμῳδο-λοιχέω, (λείχω) to play the parasite and buffoon, Ar.

κωμωδοποιοσ.gloss: a maker of comedies, comic poet
κωμωδοποιοσ.def: κωμῳδο-ποιός, οῦ, ὁ, a maker of comedies, comic poet, Plat.

κωμωδοσ.def: κωμ-ῳδός, οῦ, ὁ, (v. κωμῳδία) a comedian, i. e., 1. a comic actor, Xen., Aeschin. 2. a comic poet, Plat.

κωνειον.def: κώνειον, ου, τό, hemlock, Lat. cicuta:—hemlock-juice, by which criminals were put to death at Athens, Ar., etc.

κωνιον.def: κωνίον, ου, τό, (Dim. of κῶνος) a small cone, Anth.

κωνιτισ.def: κωνῖτις, ιδος (κῶνος I) extracted from pine-cones, Anth.

κωνοσ.def: κῶνος, ου, I. the fruit of the πεύκη, a pine-cone, Theocr., etc. II. a cone, Lat. conus, in Mathematics, Arist. 2. the cone of a helmet, Anth.

κωνοτομεω.def: κωνο-τομέω, to make a conic section, Anth.

κωνοφοροσ.def: κωνο-φόρος, ον (φέρω) bearing a cone, Anth.

κωνωπειον.gloss: an Egyptian couch with mosquito-curtains; conopium
κωνωπειον.def: κωνωπεῖον, ου, τό, (κώνωψ) an Egyptian couch with mosquito-curtains; conopium in Hor.

κωνωψ.def: κώνωψ, ωπος, a gnat, mosquito, Lat. culex, Hdt., Aesch., etc.

κωοσ.gloss: of, from the island Cos, Coan
κωοσ.def: Κῷος, η, ον (Κῶς) I. of, from the island Cos, Coan, Hdt. II. as Subst., Κῷος (sc. βόλος), the highest throw with the ἀστράγαλοι, v. Χῖος.

κωπαισ.def: Κωπαίς 1. of or near Copae (in Boeotia), ἡ Κ. λίμνη lake Copais Strab. 2. ἐγχέλεις Κωπαΐδες eels from lake Copais, Ar.

κωπευσ.gloss: pieces of wood fit for making oars, oar-spars
κωπευσ.def: κωπεύς, έως, only in pl. κωπέες, attic κωπῆς, pieces of wood fit for making oars, oar-spars, Hdt., Ar., etc.

κωπευω.def: κωπεύω, (κώπη) to propel with oars, Anth.

κωπη.def: κώπη, ἡ, (from Root ΚΑΠ, Lat. capio) any handle: 1. the handle of an oar, and generally an oar, Od., Pind., attic; νερτέρᾳ προσήμενος κώπῃ, θαλαμίτης, metaph. of a man of low rank, Aesch.; παραπέμπειν ἐφ’ ἕνδεκα κώπαις, a proverb of dub. origin, meaning "to escort with all the honours, " Ar.:—poet. to express ships, σὺν κώπᾳ χιλιοναύτᾳ, of Agamemnon's fleet, Eur. 2. the handle of a sword, the haft, hilt, Lat. capulus, Hom., Soph. 3. the handle of a key, Od. 4. the haft of a torch, Eur.

κωπηλατεω.def: κωπηλᾰτέω, to pull an oar: metaph. of any similar motion forwards and backwards, as of a carpenter using an auger, Eur. (from κωπηλᾰ́της)

κωπηλατησ.def: κωπ-ηλᾰ́της, ου, ὁ, (ἐλαύνω) a rower, Polyb.

κωπηρησ.def: κωπ-ήρης, ες (⁎ἄρω) I. furnished with oars, Aesch., Eur., Thuc. II. holding the oar, χείρ Eur.

κωπιον.def: κωπίον, ου, τό, (Dim. of κώπη, Ar.)

κωριον.def: κώριον, ου, τό, doric Dim. of κούρα, a little girl, Ar.

κωρυκιοσ.def: Κωρῠ́κιος, η, ον Corycian (from the Corycian cave in Mt. Parnassus), Soph.; κορυφαὶ Κ. the peaks of Parnassus, Eur.; also Κωρυκὶς, πέτρα Aesch.

κωρυκοσ.def: κώργ̆κος, ὁ, 1. a leathern sack or wallet for provisions, Od. 2. in the gymnasium, a large leathern sack hung up, filled with fig-grains (κεγχραμίδες), flour, or sand, for the athletes to strike, Arist.
Κώρῠκος, ὁ, a promontory of Cilicia, Hhymn., Thuc.

κωσ.def: Κῶς the island Cos, opposite Caria, Hom.:— Κόωνδε to Cos, Il.

κωτιλλω.def: κωτίλλω, (only in pres.) I. to prattle, chatter, Lat. garrire, mostly with notion of wheedling, Hes., Theogn., etc. II. trans. to talk over, attempt to wheedle, Theogn., Soph. (deriv. uncertain)

κωτιλοσ.def: κωτίλος, η, ον (from κωτίλλω) I. of a swallow, twittering, Anacr., etc.: of persons, chattering, prattling, babbling, Lat. garrulus, Theogn., Theocr. II. metaph. lively, expressive, Theocr., Anth.

κωφοσ.def: κωφός, ή, όν (κόπτω) I. radical sense, blunt, dull, obtuse, κωφὸν βέλος the blunt, dull shaft, opp. to ὀξύ, Il. II. metaph.: 1. dumb, mute, κύματι κωφῷ with dumb wave, before it breaks, id.; κωφὴν γαῖαν ἀεικίζει dishonours the dumb, senseless earth, id.; τὰ μὲν ἄλλα ἔσκε κωφά the other parts of the ground sounded dull, opp. to the ringing of the hollow parts, Hdt.; ὁ κ. λιμήν, prob. the bay of Munychia, as opp. to the noisy Peiraeus, Xen. 2. after Hom., of men, dumb, Orac. ap. Hdt.: deaf and dumb, id. 3. deaf, Lat. surdus, Hhymn., Aesch., etc. 4. of the mind, dull, stupid, Lat. fatuus, Soph.; also senseless, unmeaning, κ. καὶ παλαί’ ἔπη id.

κωφοτησ.def: κωφότης, ητος, (from κωφός) deafness, Plat., Dem., etc.
